title: friction-harvest-memo-and-priority-resolve-2026-04-02
content:
Purpose
---
This working memo synthesizes a recent tranche of customer feedback touching runtime friction and feature asks. It is intentionally raw: prioritized asks, quick mitigation ideas, signal provenance, and recommended next steps for a set of low-cost probes we can ship within a sprint.

Context and signal sources (last 6 weeks)
- Enterprise accounts (3): latency spikes for medium-length chat sessions when customers use streaming + tools. Two accounts filed high-severity support tickets (JIRA-1289, JIRA-1290).
- Three PLG customers reported repeated "hallucination"-like failures when model fallback to smaller quantized variant happened during burst events.
- Field notes from Solutions Eng (Slack thread: #cs-runtime) indicating confusion about cache invalidation behavior after prompt templating changes.
- Observability spikes: console traces show KV-cache churn correlated with a subset of customers that use long history + incremental prompt edits.

Raw asks (verbatim snippets)
- "We need predictable tail latency when a user is editing a long chat, otherwise UX is broken."
- "Why did the model change from v1 to v1-quant during our run? We saw output style change and lost context."
- "Cache seems to serve stale prefixed tokens sometimes after we update system prompts."

Synthesis: themes and causal hypotheses
1) Latency fragility at tail under combined streaming + large history. Hypothesis: continuous batching triggers kernel-selection path that doesn't meet per-token SLOs for streaming; fallback to quantized models increases variance.
2) KV-cache semantics mismatch. Hypothesis: customers expect prefix-level cache invalidation to be explicit; current automatic prefix caching is opaque and occasionally holds outdated system prompt fragments.
3) Rollout/fallback observability blind spots. Hypothesis: when routing policy falls back to quantized variant, clients are not given clear telemetry that explains the change in model variant (only internal logs).

Priority-resolve matrix (quick view)
- P0 (customer-impact + low-effort probe): explicit cache-invalidation API + client-visible cache status header (ETA: patch, 1 sprint) — owner: Arjun Patel.
- P1 (medium effort, high signal): streaming per-token SLO enforcement and a diagnostics mode to surface when batching delays exceed threshold (ETA: 2 sprints) — owner: Lina Chen.
- P2 (investigate, informs policy): enhance routing transparency: expose fallback events as typed telemetry plus optional client callback (ETA: research spike 1 sprint) — owner: Dmitri Sokolov.

Cost/benefit quick notes
- Cache-invalidation API: low dev effort, high perceived reliability improvement for customers that do prompt engineering in prod. Potential downside: more invalidations could reduce hit rates; recommend a soft-rate-limit with server-side heuristics.
- Per-token SLO enforcement in streaming: higher complexity (runtime/kernel selection). Benefit: reduced observed tail latency and fewer replays from clients. Consider a staged rollout behind a feature flag.
- Routing transparency: minimal runtime changes (emit events), but requires SDK surface changes and docs. High ROI for debuggability.

Concrete probe designs (lean experiments we can ship fast)
Probe A — "invalidate-prefix" API (P0)
- Short description: a simple endpoint that accepts session_id + prefix_hash and forces eviction of prefix entries in KV cache for that session.
- Success metric (customer): 80% reduction in reported "stale prompt" incidents from pilot customers.
- Internal metric: cache-hit delta and CPU usage delta for pilot group.
- Risks/notes: need to throttle to avoid cache stampede; default to no-op for Dedicated customers unless explicitly enabled.

Probe B — streaming diagnostics header (P0/P1 hybrid)
- Short description: attach a periodic header to streaming responses with a small diagnostics blob: {batch_wait_ms, kernel_path, fallback_flag}. Blob should be base64-encoded to avoid protocol bloat.
- Success metric: number of support calls answered without escalations due to attached header increases by 40%.
- Privacy note: ensure header contains no PII and respects data retention policy.

Probe C — fallback telemetry + opt-in callback (P1)
- Short description: when routing policy switches model variant mid-request, emit a typed event to customer webhook (opt-in) and to console logs. Include reason code and latency/cost delta.
- Success metric: pilot customers enable webhook and report faster RCA.

Implementation checklist (first two sprints)
- Sprint 1: design API + sequence diagrams for invalidate-prefix; implement server-side handler + simple SDK shim returning a boolean. Build initial acceptance tests. Owner: Arjun.
- Sprint 1: add streaming diagnostics header, but gated behind a feature-flag per-tenant. Owner: Lina.
- Sprint 2: roadmap discussion with platform-eng to add typed fallback events and webhook plumbing. Owner: Dmitri.

Open questions / items for engineering review
- Should invalidate-prefix be session-scoped only or allow broader keys? (tradeoff: power vs. blast radius).
- How to represent prefix identity (hash scheme)? Compatibility with existing KV cache keys.
- Performance cost: measure worst-case invalidation QPS needed for a pilot of 10 high-activity customers.
- Telemetry schema: propose minimal typed event format (event_type, session_id, reason_code, model_prev, model_new, latency_ms). Need feedback from observability team.

Notes to self / follow-ups
- Capture a short demo checklist for CS engineers so they can exercise the invalidate-prefix flow (include curl examples).
- Draft a short customer-facing explanation note that explains why fallback may happen and how to opt into improved telemetry.
- Coordinate with Console PM to add a per-tenant toggle for streaming diagnostics header and fallback webhook opt-in.

Appendix: pilot candidate customers and sample transcripts
- Pilot A (enterprise fin-saas): heavy long-form conversation; average conversation length 1.6k tokens; reported user-visible stalls ~ 2–3x per 1000 requests. Contact: Tom B. (acct team).
- Pilot B (midmarket research tool): uses prompt templates that get updated frequently; reported stale system prompt fragments after template change. Contact: Priya S.
- Example transcript snippet (anonymized):
  - user: "update the system prompt to 'speak more formally'"
  - subsequent request: "assistant starts using old tone"
  - engineering observation: cache returned prefixed embeddings that included earlier prompt variant.

Quick decision guidance (for PM loop)
- Ship Probe A (invalidate-prefix) now as a high-confidence low-risk mitigation. Communicate to Customer Success and Solutions Eng with a short playbook.
- Start Sprint 1 work on streaming diagnostics header gated behind feature-flag. Re-run workload benchmarks with 4 representative kernels.
- Schedule an 30-min sync with Observability + Platform Eng to finalize telemetry schema (blocker: none if we emit logs; blocker if we require new high-cardinality indices).

End of memo.
